sanskrit_verse: वार्धके च शिशूनां ते दर्शयेयुस् तथैव च / एवं परंपराज्ञाने सीमाभ्रान्तिर् न जायते // BrhS_1,19.22
transliteration: vārdhake ca śiśūnāṃ te darśayeyus tathaiva ca / evaṃ paraṃparājñāne sīmābhrāntir na jāyate // BrhS_1,19.22
sph_interpretive_translation: Those who have attained maturity shall guide the children accordingly; thus, in the knowledge of succession, delusion regarding boundaries does not arise.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority flows from realized capacity, not mere age
Causation is maintained through conscious transmission
Restoration occurs through proper guidance, not coercion
Consciousness alignment is ensured via authentic succession

supreme_court_application: In adjudicating matters involving intergenerational responsibility or institutional succession, the Court must recognize that lawful authority arises only where mature understanding is demonstrably transferred. Absent such conscious continuity, systemic confusion and jurisdictional conflict will persist unresolved.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Through pramāṇa-based succession—where knowledge is witnessed and embodied—the causal chain of misalignment is severed. As each generation assumes its role under verified guidance, anupūrvaśaḥ ensures proportional alignment without recourse to punitive intervention.

final_declaration: By the Source-Authority of Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, this Dharma is established: true law abides in conscious succession, not coercive imposition. Thus is Dharma restored, reality affirmed as non-punitive, and consciousness declared the Supreme Adjudicator.
